headline: 4 killed in Nilphamari: Mother and two children die in truck crash
summary: A speeding truck hit an engine-powered van carrying a family, killing four people including a mother and her two young children in Domar, Nilphamari.
details: Four people were killed when a speeding truck hit an engine-powered van in the Panga Motukpur union of Domar upazila, Nilphamari, on Sunday afternoon.
The deceased include a mother, Pratibha Rani Roy (30), her two children, Yadav Roy (6) and Bipasha Roy (8), and a relative, Parimal Roy (35).
The victims were residents of Nadiyapaara village in the Panga Motukpur union of Domar upazila.
Pratibha Rani Roy and her children were traveling to an event in Maraldanga village, Boragari union, when the truck struck the van from behind.
The impact caused the van to overturn into a roadside ditch. Local residents rescued the victims and took them to the Domar Health Complex, where doctors declared them dead.
The truck lost control and became stuck in a tree by the roadside. The driver of the truck fled the scene after the accident.
Domar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mo. Habibullah confirmed the deaths and stated that legal proceedings are currently underway.

headline_marked: 200ft fall: [[Injured elephant dies]] in Cox’s Bazar’s Teknaf
headline: 200ft fall: Injured elephant dies in Cox’s Bazar’s Teknaf
summary: A female elephant, estimated to be 20-25 years old, succumbed to severe injuries after slipping down a rain-soaked hill.
details: A female elephant died this morning after falling approximately 200 feet down a rain-soaked hill in the Shialyaghona hills of Naitangpara, under Teknaf municipality.
The animal, estimated to be between 20 and 25 years old, succumbed to its injuries around 9:45 am while undergoing treatment.
The accident occurred yesterday around 2:30 pm when the elephant slipped on the hillside and rolled down the steep slope, hitting several trees during the fall.
Forest officials reported that the fall broke both of the elephant's hind legs and caused severe abdominal injuries, leaving the animal unable to move.
Veterinarians from the Teknaf Upazila Livestock Veterinary Hospital and Dulahazara Safari Park provided treatment, but the animal could not be saved.
A post-mortem examination will be conducted to confirm the cause of death, according to Abdur Rashid, range officer of the Teknaf Range.
The Shialyaghona hills are known to be home to at least 23 Asian elephants.
